questions.question: Explain the economic significance of hinterlands connections for port cities. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Hinterlands provided raw materials, markets, and labour. Integration of local economy
  • to the global. Patterns of exploitation. Growth of infrastructure and colonial trade.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How did architectural styles reflect colonial cultural policies? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Colonial architecture as expression of authority and cultural hierarchy. Use of neo
  • classical style- parallels with imperial Rome- order and power- selective appropriation
  • of local style- imperial benevolence and legitimation.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: In what ways did spaces like railway stations and regimental bazaars become sites for both reinforcing and quietly subverting colonial racial zoning / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Spaces of segregation- railway stations and bazars as spaces of contact- cross cultural
  • encounters- erosion of racial boundaries.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain how epidemics could strengthen state power as well as provoke resistance. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Epidemics and expansion of state authority through surveillance, compulsory
  • measures and public health institutions, consolidating administrative reach. Intrusion
  • into personal life, economic dislocation and disrespect for local practices.
  • Contestations and popular resistance.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain why traditional healers persisted despite colonial suppression. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Inaccessibility of colonial medicine- failure to culturally legitimate treatment-
  • existence of local belief systems- distrust of British- efforts at cultural revival as part
  • of nationalism.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain why the forced examination of women provoked strong resistance during plague control. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Forced examinations- violated norms of bodily modesty and privacy,
  • disproportionately targeted women, and signalled colonial disrespect- provoking
  • anger, loss of dignity and organised resistance.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Assess the cultural consequences of moving from direct colonial rule to global economic systems. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Dispersal of imperial economic linkages into multinational corporations and market
  • logics. Reshaping identities and cultural practices through consumerism, media flows
  • and new labour regimes. Persistence in patterns of extraction and inequality.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Use corporate influence to illustrate trade agreements in postcolonial states. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Role of Corporations in shaping trade agreements. Lobbying for LPG, investor
  • protections and intellectual property rules. Prioritising corporate interests over social
  • policies in postcolonial states. Influencing regulatory frameworks and development
  • choices.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Evaluate how urban inequality restricts access to essential services like healthcare in global cities. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Urban inequality produces spatial and economic exclusion - informal settlements lack
  • infrastructure and residents face financial and bureaucratic barriers- which reduces
  • healthcare access despite proximity to advanced medical facilities.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is meant by citizen science? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Citizen science- public participation in scientific research and data collection. Non-
  • specialists contribute observations, monitoring and analysis alongside professional
  • researchers- role in creating inclusive future.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Why must urban futures be rethought? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Problems with existing urban models- inequality, environmental risk and
  • infrastructural fragility. Need to rethink futures- to make cities resilient, equitable and
  • sustainable under climate change and ongoing urbanisation.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Assess whether urban resistance is effective against neoliberal reforms. / [CO4] [2x10 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Role of Urban resistance in modifying reforms through protests, legal action and
  • alternative practices. Is it effective? State coercion, fragmented movements and
  • institutional capture as limitations.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain how labour compounds were designed to control the movement and social interactions of workers in colonial India. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Conceived spaces- enclosed compounds with single entry points, segregated living
  • and work zones, curfews and pass systems. Role of paternalistic amenities and
  • surveillance in regulating social life and discouraging political organising. Effect-
  • control of labour mobility and social networks suited industrial discipline and reduced
  • collective action.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Using examples from Madras, explain how colonial planning restricted movement between Europeans and Indians. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Racial zoning- civil lines, cantonments, bazars and slums- white and black towns-
  • availability of public transport, public amenities and recreational facilities- municipal
  • regulations and policing enforced these spatial separations. Cite examples for Madras.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Describe key features of neoclassical and Indo-Saracenic architectural styles. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Neoclassical- symmetry, columns, pediments, imperial grandeur and reference to
  • Roman power. Indo-Saracenic- fusion with domes, arches, chhatris and ornament
  • drawn from Indo-Islamic tradition combined with Victorian elements. Necessity-
  • symbolic messages of power along with the message of accommodation of local
  • traditions.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the connection between data collection and surveillance. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Data collection- censuses, health reports, maps etc. - role in knowledge production- to
  • monitor populations, manage resources and target interventions. Role in enabling
  • control, exclusion and administrative power. Consequence- administrative reach and
  • social classification.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Describe how health certificates for pilgrims were implemented and enforced. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Role of colonial powers in identifying pilgrims with events of epidemic
  • dissemination- medical inspection and certificates - local health officers issued
  • certificates after checks- enforcement relied on travel restrictions- fines or denial of
  • entry to pilgrimage sites. How power reframed ways of life.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Describe how colonial authorities justified demolition of houses in the name of hygiene. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Epidemics as tools of surveillance and control- weaponisation of public health and
  • sanitation- overcrowding and unsanitary structures spread disease- demolition as
  • scientifically necessary- targeted marginal communities and ignored structural causes.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Evaluate the role of neoliberal governance in empowering postcolonial subjectivities. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Neoliberal governance- fosters entrepreneurial subjectivities- lessons on self-
  • responsibility and flexibility- opportunities for consumer identity and new
  • professional classes. Problems- marginalises those lacking capital, reshaping
  • citizenship into market participation, divorces governments from societal
  • responsibility.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Evaluate the equity of structural adjustment policies in promoting sustainable development. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Structural adjustment and smuggling of capitalism- fiscal austerity and liberalisation-
  • undermining of public services and social safety nets- short-term macroeconomic
  • gains but long-term inequities.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Analyse how impact assessments balance growth and environmental protection. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Impact assessments- to identify environmental costs and mitigation- a procedural
  • mechanism to temper growth. Role of independence, data quality and enforcement in
  • its effectiveness — they can be box-ticking unless backed by political will.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Examine how popular culture reproduces or challenges imperial afterlives. / [CO4] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Popular culture- films, music, festivals- role in reproducing imperial legacies. Their
  • role in subverting narratives - foregrounding subaltern voices and creating
  • counterhistories.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Consider the significance of Fort St George as a prototype for British colonial urban planning in India. To what extent did it establish enduring patterns of spatial segregation? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Fort St George- established in 1640 by EIC on the Coromandel Coast- role as
  • administrative and military nucleus of early British authority- an example of colonial
  • urban formations. Conceived as a fortress-city- spatial logic that combined
  • commercial, military, and political functions within a rigidly segregated urban layout.
  • The design of the town- white and black towns. Spatial division symbolised-security
  • concerns and racial hierarchy that was central to imperial urban ideology.
  • Contestation of these patterns- indigenous settlement logics, economic imperatives,
  • and local governance practices- softened rigid segregation in practice.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Critically assess the claim that colonial public health measures were tools of racial governance rather than purely medical responses. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Colonial public health- medical rationality and the logic of political control. Medicine
  • and racial underpinnings of imperial governance. Role in policing and regulating the
  • colonised population. Measure of regulation and surveillance. Prioritising the
  • protection of European enclaves. Racial hierarchies of operation- differential access
  • to hospitals, segregated wards, and the enforcement of sanitation norms. Examples
  • from colonial cities. Biopolitical control and its justification through scientific
  • discourse. Colonial power and its reach into everyday life.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Critique the role of global markets in sustaining colonial economic dependencies. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Role of global markets in perpetuating structural dependencies. Colonialism and
  • organisation of economic systems around the export of raw materials and the import
  • of manufactured goods. World System Theory. Decolonisation- LPG and
  • corporations- reproduction of asymmetries- birth of competition states. competition
  • states- industrialisation, protectionist measures, and regional cooperation to mitigate
  • dependency. South-South solidarity.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Demonstrate how speculative futures have been integrated into urban planning practices. / [CO4] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Speculative futures- grounded in projections, predictive models, and financial
  • expectations- have become central to contemporary urban planning. Reframes the city
  • as an investment prospect- land banking, SEZ, PPP, Smart City- blending
  • technological optimism with financial rationalisation. Areas of concerns- marginalise
  • existing communities and exacerbate socio-spatial inequalities, neglect ecological and
  • cultural dimensions.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
